[ This is a sealed-bid second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values and one round. The dominant strategy is to bid my true value because my bid affects only whether I win, not the price paid (which is the second-highest bid). Bidding $38 maximizes expected profit: I win whenever competitors’ max bid is below 38 and pay that competing bid. Tie-breaking is random; truthful bidding remains optimal. No benefit to shading in a second-price auction. ]

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth if the second-highest bid exceeds your value; underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. With no useful history and ties random, the best long-run profit strategy is truthful bidding. Therefore, bid exactly your value of $12 (in 0.1 increments allowed). ]
